page: Amazon Web Services c7gn.medium is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by an arm64-based AWS Neoverse-V1 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz. The instance provides 1 dedicated vCPU spanning 1 physical core and 1 thread per core. Memory capacity is configured at 2.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The CPU cache architecture provides 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptographic acceleration. There is no integrated local storage or hardware GPU acceleration, requiring reliance on external network storage. Network interfaces provide a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations highlight balanced single-threaded execution alongside strict resource boundaries. In single-core testing, the instance registers average relative performance with a stress-ng score of 1516.59 and a Geekbench score of 1500.0. Multi-core benchmark scores effectively match single-core measurements, recording 1502.0 on Geekbench and 1516.59 on stress-ng, reflecting the single-threaded capacity. Memory bandwidth benchmarks yield 31.16 GB/sec for uncached large reads and 11.03 GB/sec for large writes. Application benchmarks demonstrate 1.71 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 1.91 GB/sec, while a small 135M LLM model processes 56.13 generation tokens per second.

The primary tradeoff of c7gn.medium is its single-core and 2.0 GB memory envelope, which limits high-concurrency or memory-intensive deployments. However, it delivers strong cost efficiency for lightweight workloads that benefit from dedicated arm64 execution and 3 Gbps baseline networking. Appropriate workloads include microservices, edge routing, small containerized background tasks, lightweight CI/CD worker steps, and arm64 development environments.
description: Amazon Web Services c7gn.medium is an entry-level compute-optimized instance powered by a dedicated 1-vCPU AWS Neoverse-V1 ARMv8 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz. Operating on the AWS Nitro system, it includes 2.0 GB of memory, 32 MB of L3 cache, and AES instruction set support. The instance includes no bundled local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, delivering 3 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate average single-threaded capability, demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 1500.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 1516.59. Multi-core performance scales predictably with the single vCPU configuration, producing a static web throughput of 1.91 GB/sec and 1.71 million Redis SET operations per second. The c7gn.medium is suited for lightweight arm64 services, network proxies, small background processors, and development tasks.
